headline: Mozambique Protects Mount Mabu's Butterfly Forest and 200 Endemic Species
meta_description: Mozambique has designated 23,000 acres as a protected conservation area to safeguard Mount Mabu's 200+ butterfly species and rare forest ecosystem.
summary_short: Mozambique just protected 23,000 acres of Mount Mabu, a biodiverse mountain forest home to 200+ butterfly species found nowhere else on Earth.
body:
On August 24th, Mozambique's government issued a historic decree establishing the Mount Mabu Community Conservation Area across 23,000 acres, securing the future of one of southern Africa's most remarkable ecosystems. The protected zone encompasses what naturalist Sir David Attenborough famously called the "butterfly forest"—a rainforest-covered mountain chain harboring over 200 butterfly species, many found nowhere else in the world. This decision matters because Mount Mabu and its neighboring Mount Namuli represent possibly the largest continuous block of medium-altitude forest in southern Africa, and decades of researcher Julian Bayliss's work have revealed species entirely new to science, including the Mount Mabu forest viper. The mountains' extreme isolation has created an ecosystem where endemism runs high—meaning species thrive here and almost nowhere else.

What makes this protection especially meaningful is Mozambique's journey. For decades after independence, the nation's civil war left parks depleted and wildlife populations devastated by unchecked poaching. Now at peace, the country faces a choice: rebuild what was lost, or protect what remains. This decree prioritizes prevention. The Ministry of Agriculture, Environment, and Fisheries has designed the reserve to balance "protection, conservation and sustainable use of natural resources by local communities"—and community buy-in appears strong, as locals already consider these mountains sacred.

Mozambique's broader conservation efforts are gaining momentum. Since the civil war ended, the nation has established numerous protected spaces, and today 25 percent of the country's territory is preserved in some form. A community management plan for Mount Mabu is now being developed, suggesting that this forest—and its 200 butterfly species—will be safeguarded not just by law, but through the stewardship of those who call it home.
quick_facts: 23,000 acres designated as Mount Mabu Community Conservation Area on August 24th
Over 200 butterfly species call Mount Mabu home, most found nowhere else
Sir David Attenborough named it the "butterfly forest" in 2013 BBC presentation
Possibly largest continuous medium-altitude forest block in southern Africa
25% of Mozambique's national territory now protected in some form
